subject: humanities
passage: After completing the tone poem Tapiola in 1926, the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius published no further major work, although he lived for thirty-one more years at Ainola, his house north of Helsinki. Throughout the 1930s, conductors and publishers waited for an Eighth Symphony that he repeatedly promised and repeatedly withheld; his family later recalled that he burned a pile of manuscripts in the 1940s, and the symphony, if it was ever finished, has not survived. The decades of silence turned a composer ______ many listeners had assumed was simply enjoying a long retirement into a figure of fascination, and what he wrote and destroyed in those years still occupies scholars.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: Set aside the inserted phrase "many listeners had assumed" and the clause reads "who was simply enjoying a long retirement." The pronoun is the subject of the verb "was enjoying," so it takes the subject form "who." The words "many listeners had assumed" do not make the pronoun an object.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Whose" shows possession, but nothing in the clause belongs to the composer; the clause needs a subject pronoun.
explanation.B: Correct. "Who" is the subject of "was … enjoying"; the phrase "many listeners had assumed" is a parenthetical insertion that does not change the pronoun's case.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Whom" is an object form, but the pronoun is the subject of "was … enjoying"; "many listeners had assumed" is only an insertion, and "assumed" does not take the pronoun as its object.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Which" refers to things, not to a person such as the composer.
